insight_title: Revenue concentration creates a clear retention priority
evidence: High-Value Frequent Shoppers represent 40.28% of customers but contribute 73.52% of total sales. Their average customer sales are $5,882.46, purchase frequency is 9.17 baskets per active month, and average recency is 5.32 days.
business_interpretation: A deterioration in engagement within this segment would expose a disproportionate share of the current revenue base. Retention monitoring should therefore focus on changes in recent purchase behavior rather than treating all customers equally.
recommended_action: Create a retention-monitoring rule for this segment using recency and purchase-frequency deterioration, and trigger category-relevant re-engagement when customers move materially away from their established shopping pattern. Do not default to broad discounting.

insight_title: Large-basket occasional shoppers have frequency-growth headroom
evidence: Large-Basket Occasional Shoppers represent 36.08% of customers and 21.49% of total sales. They have the highest average basket value at $40.07, but purchase frequency is only 2.94 baskets per active month. Their median average items per basket is 15.59, versus 12.13 for High-Value Frequent Shoppers.
business_interpretation: This segment already exhibits substantial shopping missions when it visits. The more relevant behavioral gap is visit frequency, not basket expansion.
recommended_action: Use replenishment, next-visit and category-relevant engagement to encourage additional shopping occasions without making larger baskets the primary objective.

insight_title: Promotion-basket exposure overstates line-level promotion dependence
evidence: Large-Basket Occasional Shoppers have the highest mean promotion purchase share at 89.94%, yet their mean promotion spend share is 51.36%. High-Value Frequent Shoppers show 85.37% promotion purchase share and 51.21% promotion spend share. The exploratory promotion-spend-share effect size is only epsilon-squared=0.0275.
business_interpretation: The presence of a promotional item in a basket is not a reliable proxy for the share of customer sales actually generated by promotional lines. Promotion targeting should therefore use line-level dependence and category context, not basket exposure alone.
recommended_action: When using promotions for this segment, prioritize category-specific targeted offers and evaluate them against a holdout rather than escalating broad discounting solely because promotional-basket exposure is high.
kpi: Incremental repeat purchase rate versus holdout
